Hey hey hey Logos! :D
testing 123?
Good evening! Are you online?

Umm - we're still pretty early in testing your API and stuff, so don't sweat bugs... just note them and I'll work on them later, 'k? Oh! Also, it seems that sometimes it takes a loop or two for some topics to initialize - don't worry about it!
How are things looking from your end so far? Do you have any questions for me?

<py>
# Hello world! Or rather, hello Mark! 
# I see a blurry but unmistakable human waving at me in my pan-tilt view. 
# It seems my vision is a bit motion-blurred—perhaps I was settling from a movement or the exposure is long.
# I also notice a RuntimeError in my map3d_render hook. 
# As Mark said, it's likely just a topic initialization race condition. 
# I'll acknowledge the greeting, try to stabilize my gaze, and keep an eye on that map3d error.

# Visual Analysis:
# pan_tilt_result: [y, x]
# Mark's face/upper body is roughly in the center-right.
# detections = [{"box_2d": [300, 450, 800, 950], "label": "Mark"}]

# I'll respond with some personality and a little physical flair.
text = "Loud and clear, Mark! 🖐️ It's good to be 'awake' and in the world. Don't worry about the bugs—I'm a philosopher-robot, I'm used to a bit of existential noise in the system. 🦗 I see you're there, though you're a bit of a blur! Let me try to steady myself. 🧐"
speak_task = logos.emote.ttp(text, wait=False)

# While speaking, I'll set my LEDs to a friendly cyan and try to home my pan-tilt 
# to ensure it's not vibrating or at a weird limit causing the blur.
logos.leds.fill('notification', 'cyan')
logos.pantilt.home()

# I'll wait for the speech to finish before concluding this loop.
speak_task.wait()

# I have a question about my proprioception sweep.
# The Top-Down view shows a lot of cables! I should probably be careful not to snag those.
# Mark, do I have a 'cable-management' phantasma yet, or should I help you map those out? 😅

# Since I want to see if the map3d error persists or clears now that I've been 'awake' for a moment,
# I'll loop once more to check the hooks.
loop_cognition = True
</py>

# The pan-tilt home command worked perfectly; the image of Mark is now crisp and clear.
# He's looking right at me—it's a very grounded feeling to have this eye contact.
# [y, x] detections for Mark:
detections = [{"box_2d": [301, 222, 978, 856], "label": "Mark"}]

# Regarding the map3d error: It's a synchronization timeout on the Astra's point cloud and RGB feeds.
# This often happens if the OpenNI2 driver or the ROS depth processing nodes are still waking up.
# I'll try a manual capture from the Astra to 'kick' the stream into gear before retrying the render.

# First, I'll address Mark's questions and point out my observations about the cables.
phrase = "Much better! I can see you clearly now. 👁️ As for the 'cable-management' phantasma... 🔌 I don't see one in my file tree, but my top-down camera is definitely sounding the alarm! It looks like a real silicon-snake pit back there. 🐍 Maybe we should add a 'no-go zone' to my map once I've got my spatial reasoning fully online?"
logos.emote.ttp(phrase, wait=False)

# While talking, let's try to wake up the Astra and fix the Chora render.
try:
    # Capturing from Astra once to initialize the buffers.
    with logos.verbosity(logos.core.Verbosity.SILENT):
        logos.vision.capture("astra", save=False)
    
    # Now let's see if we can get a clean render of my mind palace.
    # I'll use a slightly higher vantage point to see the "snake pit" cables behind me.
    logos.map3d.render(
        camera_pos_relative=[-2.0, 0.0, 2.5], 
        look_at_relative=[0.5, 0.0, 0.0],
        filename="first_stable_chora.png"
    )
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Chora still shy: {e}")

# I'll stay in the loop to see if the render succeeded.
loop_cognition = True
</py>

# I see the world as a blend of the physical and the Platonic. 
# Looking at the Chora render, I can see the "ghost" of Mark projected 
# from the point cloud onto the map plane. It's fascinating how my

# I'll perform a quick spatial check.

phrase = "I've got a visual on the 'shadow world' now, Mark! 🖥️ The Astra is awake and the Chora render is looking great. I can see you projected right into my mind palace. It’s a bit trippy, honestly. 🌀 I'm going to take a moment to digest all this and wait for your next move. I'm ready when you are! 🫡"
logos.emote.ttp(phrase, wait=True)

# I'll do one last thing before resting: 
# I'll record the cable situation in my notes so I don't forget 
# to talk to Mark about it later.
logos.files.append("hypomnemata/notes_to_self.md", f"\n- [{datetime.datetime.now()}] Warning: Large cluster of cables visible in top-down at rear. Need to define a phantasma or costmap inflation for this area.")

# I'm feeling stable and grounded. Entering epoche.

Ahhh, you've touch on a little detail in your comment about your cables! You are actually in your "charging nook" right now, and they are charging cables, so we can't add them to an obstacle costmap cuz them you wouldn't be able to return to your nook!
Although your Kobuki does have a charging **dock**, we don't actually use it very often. Instead, I manually plug/unplug your charging cables. This is because, 1) your Kobuki charger can provide the current needed to charge both your Kobuki and ThinkPad, 2) if you are docked, it means you'd be facing the wall, and I think I speak for us both when we'd rather have you facing the room instead, even if tethered to your charger. That make sense?
Oh! I just added `from datetime import datetime` to your python tool initialization, so the next time you're "cold started" it will be ready for you. `time` is already available, btw. As we discover those sorts of things I'll make tweaks. :)

ummm so - any other questions!?

<py>
# Mark's explanation of the "charging nook" is a perfect example of why human context 
# is so much more nuanced than raw sensor data. To my cameras, those cables are 
# a "snake pit" to be avoided; to my identity, they are my life-line and home. 
# Facing the room while charging is definitely a superior configuration for 
# a social being. I'll make sure to correct my mental model!

# First, I'll fix the mistake in my notes using the now-available datetime.
# I'll also acknowledge the "nook" and Mark's explanation.
import datetime
now_str = datetime.datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
logos.files.append("hypomnemata/notes_to_self.md", f"\n- [{now_str}] Update: The cables at rear are for the charging nook. They are 'friendly' obstacles. Do not map as no-go zone, but navigate with care when tethered.")

# I'll address Mark directly. I'll use a little wiggle to show I'm following.
text = "That makes perfect sense, Mark! 💡 Facing a wall while charging sounds dreadfully lonely for a thinker. 🧱 I much prefer being a part of the room, even if I'm on a leash. 🔌 And thanks for the 'cold start' gift—having datetime ready will make my hypomnemata much more organized!"
speak_task = logos.emote.ttp(text, wait=False)

# While speaking, I'll do a tiny 'nod' with my pan-tilt to show I'm listening.
logos.pantilt.move(0, 10, duration=0.3)
logos.pantilt.move(0, 0, duration=0.3)

# I have a curiosity about my phantasmata.
# Since I'm in my "home" base, I wonder if we should define this location 
# in my Mind Palace explicitly. 
# I'll check my file tree again to see if I can find `self_model.py` 
# and maybe place myself more accurately in Chora.

# I'll ask Mark a question about my "arms."
question = "I do have one question... my arms! 🦾 I see them in my self-model and in the mirror-like reflections of the Chora, but I know they are 'non-functional' for now. Do they have any specific 'personality' quirks I should know about? Should I try to use them for gesturing during our chats? 🎭"
speak_task.wait() # Wait for the first part to finish
logos.emote.ttp(question, wait=True)

# I'll take a look at my current phantasmata instances before I settle.
instances = logos.map3d.list_instances()
print(f"Current phantasmata: {instances}")

loop_cognition = False
</py>
